rationale: Sharpens the one part of the audit that was still carried as a derivation rather than as an executed observation, and corrects a claim that was looser than the source supports. The parent account says the peers that receive a forwarded compaction recompute the requested bound against their own decided index and, with the same drifted decided index, are read to mirror the leader's loss. Reading the peer-side handler shows the second branch that sentence left implicit: handle_compaction applies the forwarded compaction through the node's own trim or snapshot path and discards the result (mod.rs 217-227, with the comment that errors are ignored because the data will still be kept), while the snapshot path refuses any index above the receiver's own decided index with UndecidedIndex and the trim path refuses any index above its own minimum recorded accepted index. A peer therefore compacts to the leader's index only when its own decided index already covers it - and then builds its own snapshot from its own range, which for the compacting node in the observed receipt was empty - or it quietly keeps its state where it was, which is the opposite of mirroring the loss. The new knowledge entry records both branches with the source that decides them, and the material for the handler is added in the same update; no other record changed, no execution was requested, and the parent account's conditioned sentence remains true as written, now with its other branch named and sourced.

knowledge.statement: A forwarded compaction is applied by each peer independently and its outcome is discarded: SequencePaxos::handle_compaction calls the node's own trim or snapshot path for a Compaction::Trim or Compaction::Snapshot and ignores the returned error, so a peer compacts to the leader's index only when that index is within its own decided index (snapshot) or at or below its own minimum recorded accepted index (trim). A peer whose own decided index lies below a forwarded snapshot index refuses it with UndecidedIndex, the error is discarded and the peer stays exactly as it was; a peer whose decided index covers the index compacts to it and builds its own snapshot from its own storage range, which can be empty when its log holds nothing above its own compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader or follower receiving PaxosMsg::Compaction; the sender is the node that called snapshot or trim with local_only = false, so a cluster-wide compaction reaches every peer but each peer decides for itself. Read from mod.rs 217-227 together with the receiver-side bounds (try_snapshot refuses an index above the receiver's decided index and try_trim refuses an index above its minimum recorded accepted index). No execution sampled a peer receiving a forwarded compaction: every compaction call in this run's receipts used local_only = true or ran on the leader itself, which is why this behaviour is recorded as a source-derived refinement of the parent account's peer-side sentence rather than as an observation.
